statement: Under prediction a grouping of participants decides how the rows are validated (whole groups kept together, internal-external validation across groups), not the model's intercepts, so fixed-effects or cluster-only adjustment is refused.
claimed_basis: audit RO-08; MODELING_SEQUENCE §2 (prediction: grouped folds and holdout, performance heterogeneity across sites)

statement: The residual energy model and the standard (nutrient plus energy) model give the same nutrient effect for any functional form, so a restricted cubic spline of the energy residual estimates the nutrient's substitution curve at fixed total energy exactly as a spline of the nutrient with energy beside it does.
regime: dietary exposure, energy adjustment, non-linear dose–response
decision: energy model for a curved exposure
claimed_basis: Willett, Howe & Kushi 1997 (Am J Clin Nutr 65:1220S).

statement: For the proportional-odds model, Wald intervals from the inverse observed information are valid for independent rows, and when rows repeat within units the CR1 sandwich over units' summed scores with a G/(G−1) correction and a t(G−1) reference gives valid 95% intervals (no interval below the unit floor).
regime: inference; ordinal outcome; independent rows or rows clustered by unit
decision: interval method for the ordinal coefficient table
claimed_basis: Cameron & Miller 2015 §VI ("at a minimum one should use the T(G − 1) distribution"); MASS::polr / statsmodels OrderedModel for the Wald case.

statement: When some group of trial participants all had the event or none did (logistic separation), the model's risks run to 0% or 100% and no finite estimate exists, so the standardized risk difference and ratio are refused.

Survey weights and PSUs given without a strata column give intervals that treat the PSUs as unstratified, which are too narrow where people were sampled in clusters, so the answer is blocked until the user attests that the table has no strata column.
regime: set_survey population with a weight and PSU but no strata

statement: Under Predict, showing the pooled cross-validated root mean squared error instead of the mean squared error never changes which family has the lower score, because the square root is increasing, so the comparison table can show either.
regime: regression outcome under prediction, comparing families by pooled cross-validated error
decision: score shown in the comparison table

statement: Under Estimate or Describe, a Belsley condition index of 30 or more with at least two model-matrix columns having variance-decomposition proportion 0.5 or more marks a near dependency among the exposure and adjustment set; when the exposure's proportions summed over those near dependencies reach 0.5, which of the dependent columns are held fixed changes what the exposure's estimate means (more exposure at fixed partners means less of what it replaces), so it is a Decide at the adjustment question and graded 'act on it'.
regime: Estimate or Describe; outcome-blind; model matrix built as the fit builds it (intercept and columns scaled to unit length, not centered); any lens
decision: Whether the collinear-predictors noticing is a Decide routed to the adjustment-set question (band 2, changes the question)
claimed_basis: Belsley, Kuh & Welsch (1980, §3.3) for the 30 and 0.5 thresholds (code comment)

statement: Under the dietary lens, when the exposure's Pearson correlation with total energy is 0.3 or more in absolute value, the choice of energy model (substitution at fixed energy versus addition) changes what the exposure's coefficient means, so the noticing is graded 'act on it' (changes the question) and decided at the energy-model question; below 0.3 no such noticing is raised.
regime: Dietary lens; exposure and an energy column both present; Estimate or Describe (also measured under Predict when the lens is dietary)
decision: Whether the energy-carries-the-nutrient noticing fires and is a Decide routed to energy_adjustment
claimed_basis: Code comment: 'BLUEPRINT §14 rule 1: a nutrient correlated with total energy at r >= 0.3 rides on it'; SURFACING_POLICY §2.1 (substitution versus addition is changes_question)

statement: For boosted trees and XGBoost, early stopping on a stopping set of a tenth of the fit's units (patience 20 or 50, up to 1,000 or 2,000 rounds) chooses the number of trees well once the plan's effective size is at least 1,500, so that the stopping set inside an inner fit holds about 100 or more units of the rarest class; below 1,500, searching the number of trees directly is better.
regime: prediction; boosted_trees, xgboost Sobol candidates; n_plan >= 1,500 (ES on) or < 1,500 (trees searched)
decision: early-stopping switch of the Sobol candidates; stopping-set share
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.2 'Early stopping' and 'Stopping set' rows (no citation); §4.1 table (patience 20 / 50, rounds 1,000 / 2,000).

statement: A cross-validated or held-out R² for a regression outcome is measured against the training rows' mean and pooled over every out-of-fold prediction.

A nutrient recorded as a percent of energy carries no constant kcal per unit, so a substitution cannot move energy through it by a factor and must use the share-of-energy scale instead; a column recorded in a non-food unit (lb, cm, years) is no amount of food energy and is refused.
decision: Refusal of a kcal-factor substitution on a %-energy or non-food-unit column.
claimed_basis: None stated beyond the docstring's reasoning.

statement: A regression-calibrated coefficient's interval must come from a bootstrap over the whole chain (resampling PSUs within strata, whole clusters, or people as the design says, and re-imputing each resample 5 times under multiple imputation); model-based intervals and Rubin's rules over each copy's model-based variance are too narrow and are refused.
decision: refusal of model_based and rubin_only intervals; how the interval is computed
claimed_basis: Keogh, Shaw & Gustafson 2020 §6.1.2; Schomaker & Heumann (Boot MI); Rao & Wu (PSU bootstrap); MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 7.
